item.text: {"search_note":"I stopped after 4 search calls. Overall read: mostly negative. 2024 contained only narrow, reactive signs of equality protection; the broader record still shows discrimination against women, religious minorities, Papuans, and LGBT people, plus a hostile environment for dissenting viewpoints.\n\nSearch gap: I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Jokowi pursued a broad, proactive equality agenda for minorities, women, or Papuans. The clearest positive item is the Paskibraka hijab correction, plus formal equality/quotas on paper. Most other 2024 evidence points the other way: persistent discrimination, coercive uniform rules, Papuan repression, and a hostile environment for unpopular viewpoints.","evidence":[{"title":"No \"hijab ban\" for Paskibraka members on I-Day: govt","publisher":"ANTARA News","date":"2024-08-14","url":"https://en.antaranews.com/news/322483/no-hijab-ban-for-paskibraka-members-on-i-day-govt","summary":"The Presidential Secretariat clarified that female Muslim Paskibraka could keep wearing hijabs during the Aug. 17 ceremony after the BPIP controversy. This is a narrow positive: the government corrected or limited a discriminatory uniform practice affecting women and religious identity.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"Indonesia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Women have formal political rights and parties face a 30% gender quota, but women remain underrepresented; ethnic Chinese are poorly represented; some local governments discriminate against religious minorities; LGBT+ people are poorly represented. This is limited positive baseline evidence, but mainly shows equality gaps rather than active protection.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"Indonesia: Jokowi’s Term Ends with a Whimper on Rights","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-01-11","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/indonesia-jokowis-term-ends-whimper-rights","summary":"HRW says Jokowi did little to address discrimination against marginalized groups; the new criminal code threatened speech, belief, association, and the rights of women, religious minorities, and LGBT people. The implementation consultations were also described as one-sided. Strong negative evidence.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"Indonesia: End Hijab-Linked Bullying in Schools","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-02-28","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/28/indonesia-end-hijab-linked-bullying-schools","summary":"HRW said the government should fully enforce the national uniform rule allowing clothing choice because girls and women were still being bullied, expelled, or pressured over hijab rules. This is strong negative evidence that equality for women was still not being protected in practice.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"Indonesia: Racism, Discrimination Against Indigenous Papuans","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-09-18","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/18/indonesia-racism-discrimination-against-indigenous-papuans","summary":"HRW says Indigenous Papuans faced longstanding racial discrimination, suppression of peaceful self-determination protests, and security-force abuses including arbitrary arrest, torture, extrajudicial killings, and forced displacement. This is the strongest negative evidence for opposition-region/minority equality.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.3","4B.4"]},{"title":"Indonesia: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-net/2024","summary":"The online environment remained hostile to unpopular viewpoints: critics, journalists, and internet users faced prosecution, harassment, and violence; Kominfo could directly restrict content without appeals; disinformation and self-censorship were common. This is strong negative evidence for protection of dissenting or marginalized viewpoints.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.6"]}]}
